tasks.short: Select machining sequences and cutting tools

steps.what: Determine machine operations and select cutting tools for the workpiece and actual setup

tasks.design: Retain sequence and tool selection with the programmer using the existing {OTHER} computer-aided manufacturing system. Native feature suggestions support the work, while setup-specific decisions remain fully counted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tool suitability depends on material, access, fixturing and actual machine condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing manufacturing software can suggest feature-based operations without proving a new local saving.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving access, stability and tool-availability constraints.

reach.learn: How actual setup affects tool choice

evidence.claim: NX CAM supports feature-based operations; this does not establish automatic suitability for the actual fixture and machine setup.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing computer-aided manufacturing system; native features are used before new software.
The programmer checks actual stock, tool inventory and setup during fully counted selection; no free available-tool flag.
This task owns substantive sequence and tool decisions; later calculation or code-generation tasks must not claim these hours again.
No changed selection process means no incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is there repeated process-selection handling beyond current native support?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0%; existing feature-suggestion runtime earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate machining parameters from job specifications

steps.what: Analyze orders, drawings and specifications and capture verified calculation inputs
Calculate dimensions, machine speeds and feed rates using specified rules and tool data
Verify calculated parameters against specifications and actual machining constraints

tasks.design: Configure native parameter calculations in {OTHER}, the existing manufacturing software. The programmer captures exact inputs and checks the results against material, tooling and machine constraints.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual calculations and parameter re-entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tool libraries and fixed machining calculations support reusable parameter preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing valid inputs and recognising unsuitable calculated recommendations.

reach.learn: How trial results challenge nominal parameters

evidence.claim: Reusable machining calculations and tool-library data can reduce repeated parameter arithmetic; local savings remain unmeasured.

assumptions: OTHER means existing computer-aided manufacturing software; native calculation and libraries come first.

In s1 the programmer captures drawing revision, units, feature dimensions/tolerances, material, selected tool geometry, tool-data version, machine limits and chosen calculation rule. Capture and verification remain in 30%; missing or conflicting values require manual engineering resolution.
Tool choice itself belongs to the separate selection task; no saving is transferred from it.
A manufacturing engineer maintains qualified library limits in 5 incremental other-role hours per 100 baseline. No free machinability or safe-feed flag.
research_questions: How much manual arithmetic remains after input capture?

incremental.description: Calculation configuration checks and extra validation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross=35%; minus 8 focal upkeep gives net 27%. Range 0-5% covers existing native calculations and difficult specifications; E1 scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify machining plan, controller profile and program inputs before writing controller programs
Write controller-language programs through the qualified postprocessor
Verify exact program semantics and store the accepted controller file and version

tasks.design: Use the qualified postprocessor in {OTHER} manufacturing software to produce controller code and store the checked version in {DOCS}. The programmer verifies semantics and simulation evidence before storage; machine execution remains a separate controlled activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual controller-code writing and repeated file handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native postprocessing can translate checked toolpaths into a specific controller dialect.
tasks.still_hard: Machine-specific cycles, offsets and postprocessor correctness.
tasks.human_edge: The programmer understands the physical meaning of generated code.

evidence.claim: Qualified native postprocessing can generate controller code from checked machining inputs; this is not automatic machine release or a measured local saving.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing manufacturing software; use its qualified postprocessor before custom code.

The programmer's completed selection, geometry and parameter tasks produce the plan before this task. In s1 they verify part/revision, units, work coordinate system, machine/controller version, toolpath version, selected tools, parameters and postprocessor version; capture is counted in 30%.

A manufacturing engineer qualifies and maintains postprocessor/controller mappings in 5 incremental other-role hours per 100 baseline. Missing or unqualified profiles stop generation for manual engineering resolution.
This task ends at stored code. Physical setup, prove-out and execution are not removed or claimed as savings; existing postprocessing runtime earns zero.
research_questions: How much hand coding remains after qualified native postprocessing?

incremental.description: Extra regression verification and version upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact controller file hash, part revision, machine/controller profile, toolpath, parameters and postprocessor version; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross=35%; minus 8 focal upkeep gives net 27%. Range 0-5% covers already automatic posting and extensive manual controller verification; E1 scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine cutting geometry and compute dimensions

steps.what: Determine reference points, machining features and constraints from verified workpiece geometry
Compute angular and linear dimensions, radii and curvatures for specified cutting paths
Verify dimensions, hole locations and cutting paths against drawings and actual setup constraints

tasks.design: Use native geometry calculation in {OTHER} after the programmer specifies datums, features and constraints. The programmer checks dimensions and path meaning before subsequent controller-program generation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated geometry arithmetic and coordinate entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native geometry functions can calculate specified dimensions consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right datums and recognising fixture or interpretation conflicts.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the intended part and actual setup.

reach.learn: How fixture conditions affect coordinate interpretation

evidence.claim: Native geometry calculation can compute specified dimensions; datum and path validity still require programmer review.

assumptions: OTHER means existing manufacturing software; test native geometry functions first.

In s1 the programmer verifies part/drawing revision, units, model scale, datums, feature locations, tolerances and fixture constraints. Capture and manual interpretation are counted in 35%; missing geometry returns for manual clarification.
Tool and sequence decisions belong to the selection task; this task owns reference and geometry decisions. Controller code is generated only after these outputs are checked.
No free structured machinability or collision-free flag; actual setup and prove-out remain outside and unchanged.
research_questions: How much geometry arithmetic remains manual after native model use?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70, gross=30%; minus 8 focal upkeep gives net 22%. Range 0-5% covers existing native calculation and complex datum interpretation; E1 scenario.

role.altitude: Machining judgement with less repeated calculation and code transcription
reach: Validate setup constraints with machinists and qualified software profiles with manufacturing engineers
role.ambitious_version: Checked inputs support repeatable calculations and code generation while physical setup and machining judgement remain explicit.
